title: Own DEFLATE decoder and ZIP reader, compared with fflate
scope: Pure-Rust DEFLATE (stored, fixed and dynamic blocks) and ZIP central-directory reader with name filtering and strict size, ratio and entry-count limits. Behaviour on valid and malformed archives matches the original's fflate unzipSync, including which inputs it refuses. Shared by io.threemf and PNG decoding.
acceptance: Generated and adversarial corpus (bombs, bad offsets and lengths, truncation, overlapping and duplicate entries, odd flags, zip64 and encrypted entries) compares fflate and Rust on accepted entries and on refusal, with exact bytes.
A deliberately wrong Rust byte is reported as a divergence; seeded mutation fuzz of archives runs through cargo xtask fuzz with zero divergences or recorded host-limit classes.
No third-party dependency; passes the P35 purity audit.

evidence.summary: fflate 0.8.3 unzipSync vs Rust: 30,000 archives (seeds 1,7,99), 0 divergences; sabotage check reports 721

open_items: Not in ci/native-suites.json: no registered case inventory; runs as an extra ignored test under cargo xtask oracle.
Not wired to cargo xtask fuzz; zip64 and encrypted entries reached only by random mutation.
Per-entry limits only; io.threemf adds the original's own limits.
Chrome execution of fflate not compared (Node 22 only).
